parts:
Hello,

I'm a first time Stan user so I might be doing something obviously stupid, but I can't seem to find the problem.  I fit a large model in Rstan, the code ran for approximately 8 hours.  The errors appear pretty harmless to me but when I look at the returned object I receive the error 'Stan model 'e3e0e19d22c8ea8ec8d41b888c7c59ca' does not contain samples.'  

I found the following statement in the Rstan manual which might be relevant.
  However, if cores > 1 and there is an error for any of the chains, then the error(s) are printed. If all chains have errors and an error occurs before or during sampling, the returned object does not contain samples. But the compiled binary object for the model is still included, so we can reuse the returned object for another sampling.

But I really don't know what that means.  Is the object that I have saved useless, or can information actually be extracted?

Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,

Jonathon O'Brien

parts:
I would suggest trying a small number of iterations in a single
chain to make sure everything's working. It's the only way you'll
be able to debug problems.

We need better methodology guidelines that try to tell users not
to run for 8 hours without testing the models and programs first.
I really hope they find a way to fix the bug that different chains
swallow errors when running in parallel.

You could also try running CmdStan, which is more robust for this
kind of thing in that it streams out draws as it goes and doesn't
swallow error messages.

- Bob

I'd strongly suggest starting with simpler models and simulated
data so you can build up confidence that the code's working, then
throw big real data sets at it.

And feel free to send your code here for comments on efficiency.
The big thing you want to do is move to the Cholesky factor
parameterization of that correlation matrix and use the _cholesky
form of the multi-normal. It's much faster and more arithmetically
stable.

- Bob

parts:
I tried to improve the processing speed by using a Cholesky factorization on the correlation matrix.  There are now two unexpected problems that I can't quite figure out.  Somehow I'm not correctly generating N(0,1) variates and every single one of my beta random variables has identical samples.  I'm at a loss to explain what's going wrong.

I am simulating Normal(0,1) random variables to be used in the transformed parameters section.  Looking at a traceplot of these values it is clear that they are not being sampled correctly.  The full code is below but the relevant call is

parameters{

real beta_pep[npep] ;  // pep effect

vector[2] alpha[nprotch] ;
.
.
.
model{
for (i in 1:nprotch){
  alpha[i] ~ normal(0,1) ;  // normal(0,1)s used to efficiently get beta
}

As I understand it I have created an array of 2 dimensional vectors.  Then my model statement calls each vector and assigns it as a normal(0,1).  Yet somehow in the sampling the first component is not a N(0,1).  I have attached an image showing a pair of the traceplots.  The second component of the vector looks fine.  Have I made a mistake in my model syntax?


One more quick question, I have created a cholesky_factor_corr[2] object.  In this dataset the correlation matrix has only 1 parameter.  Since there is only one parameter would it be better to just assign one parameter with a uniform prior and place it in a matrix, or do you still expect a speedup from the factorization?

Thanks,

Jonathon

data {
int<lower=0> npep ;
int<lower=0> N ;
int<lower=0> nprotch ;

real y[N] ;
matrix[npep,2] int_SSN ;

int<lower=1,upper=npep> opep[N] ;
int<lower=1,upper=nprotch> oprotch[N] ;

}

parameters{

real beta_pep[npep] ;  // pep effect
vector[2] alpha[nprotch] ;  // channel/prot averages independent

real<lower=0> tau ; // peptide effect var
real<lower=0> sigma ; // experimental error
vector<lower=0>[2] bsds ; // random int and slope SD

vector[2] mu_beta ;
cholesky_factor_corr[2] L ;

}

transformed parameters {
vector[2] beta[nprotch] ;
for (i in 1:nprotch){
  beta[i] = mu_beta + bsds .* (L * alpha[i]) ;  //int_SSN*beta gives the protch mean
}

}

model {
// First do parameters that effect the protein level
mu_beta ~ normal(0,10) ;

bsds ~ normal(0, 10) ; //This is a half-normal
L ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(1) ; 

for (i in 1:nprotch){
  alpha[i] ~ normal(0,1) ;  // normal(0,1)s used to efficiently get beta
}

//Now compute peptide deviations
tau ~ normal(0, 5) ;  //peptide prior
beta_pep ~ normal(0, tau) ;


//finally add it together
sigma ~ normal(0, 5) ;
for (i in 1:N)

y[i] ~ normal(beta_pep[opep[i]] + int_SSN[opep[i]] * beta[oprotch[i]], sigma) ;

}  // end model statement

generated quantities {

  vector[nprotch] ppred;
  for (i in 1:nprotch)

ppred[i] =  beta[i][1] ;

}

setwd('C:/Users/Thom6/Documents/TMTModeling/GoldStandard')

library(rstan)
library(rstudioapi)

uprot <- unique(dat$protid)
nprot <- length(uprot)
set.seed(777)
protlab <- sample(1:6, nprot, replace =T)
datlabels <- protlab[match(dat$protid, uprot)]
dat <- data.frame(dat, datlabels)

subdat <- by(dat, dat$datlabels, function(x) x)

y <- dat$lratio

npep <- length(unique(peps))
opep <- rep(NA,N)
counter <- 1
id <- peps[1]
for (i in 1:N){
  if(id == peps[i]){
    opep[i] <- counter
  }else{
    counter <- counter + 1
    opep[i] <- counter
    id <- peps[i]
  }
}

protch <- paste(dat$protid, dat$treatment)
oprotch <- as.integer(factor(protch))
nprotch <- length(unique(protch))


pepIS <- aggregate(dat$IS ~ opep, FUN = mean)

data {
int<lower=0> npep ;
int<lower=0> N ;

vector[2] mu_beta ;
cholesky_factor_corr[2] L ;

}

for (i in 1:nprotch){
  beta[i] = mu_beta + bsds .* (L * alpha[i]) ;  //int_SSN*beta gives the protch mean
}

}

// First do parameters that effect the protein level
mu_beta ~ normal(0,10) ;

bsds ~ normal(0, 10) ; //This is a half-normal

  alpha[i] ~ normal(0,1) ;  // normal(0,1)s used to efficiently get beta
}

//Now compute peptide deviations

}  // end model statement 


generated quantities {

  vector[nprotch] ppred;
  for (i in 1:nprotch)
  ppred[i] =  beta[i][1] ;

}

'  # End of STAN code

compSSN <- stan(model_code = modelText, chains = 1, iter = 1000 )
